documents.title: Annual Vacation Accrual Policy
documents.content:
Purpose: Meridian Labs provides paid vacation so that employees can rest and recharge. This policy applies to all regular full-time employees in the United States. Part-time employees working at least 20 hours per week accrue vacation on a pro-rated basis.

Accrual rates: Vacation accrues every semi-monthly pay period based on completed years of service. Employees with 0 to 2 years of service accrue 15 days (120 hours) per year, which is 1.25 days per month. Employees with 3 to 5 years of service accrue 20 days (160 hours) per year. Employees with 6 or more years of service accrue 25 days (200 hours) per year. Your accrual rate steps up on your work anniversary date.

Accrual cap: Accrual stops once your balance reaches 1.5 times your annual entitlement (22.5 days at the 15-day tier, 30 days at the 20-day tier and 37.5 days at the 25-day tier). Accrual resumes automatically when your balance drops below the cap.

Waiting period and approvals: New hires begin accruing on their first day and may use accrued vacation after 30 days of employment. Requests are submitted in the HR portal and approved by your manager. Requests of five or more consecutive days should be submitted at least 30 days in advance. Managers must respond within three business days. The company encourages every employee to take at least 10 vacation days each calendar year.

Holidays that fall during vacation are not deducted from your balance.

documents.title: Vacation Carry-Over and Payout Policy
documents.content:
Carry-over cap: Employees may carry over a maximum of 10 unused vacation days (80 hours) from one calendar year into the next. Any balance above 10 days on December 31 is forfeited, except where state law requires otherwise. Carried-over days must be used by March 31 of the new year; days that remain unused after March 31 are forfeited, which means the effective carry-over window is three months.

How to avoid losing days: Employees receive balance reminders on October 1 and December 1. Employees may request a year-end extension from their manager and HR if a business-critical project prevented them from taking time off. Extensions are granted only in writing and never exceed 30 additional days.

Payout on separation: Accrued but unused vacation is paid out in the final paycheck in states that require it (for example California, Colorado and Illinois). In all other states, unused vacation is paid out up to a maximum of 15 days when an employee leaves in good standing and provides at least two weeks of notice. Employees terminated for gross misconduct are not eligible for payout except where required by law.

Vacation cannot be cashed out during employment. Vacation days are not transferable between employees, but employees can donate up to 3 days per year to the Community Leave Bank to help colleagues facing serious family or medical emergencies.

documents.title: Sick Leave Policy
documents.content:
Entitlement: Every employee receives 10 paid sick days (80 hours) per calendar year. Sick leave is front-loaded on January 1 for existing employees. New hires receive a pro-rated grant based on their start date, rounded up to the nearest half day.

Permitted uses: Sick days may be used for your own illness, injury, medical appointments and preventive care, and to care for a family member (spouse or partner, child, parent, sibling, grandparent or a person who is like family) who is ill or needs care. Sick days may also be used for matters related to domestic violence, sexual assault or stalking, including counseling, relocation and legal proceedings.

Notification: Notify your manager as early as possible, ideally before the start of your workday, through chat, phone or email. For planned appointments, give as much notice as is practical. A doctor's note is required only after three consecutive sick days, and the note should confirm the dates of absence, not the diagnosis.

Carry-over: Up to 5 unused sick days (40 hours) carry over to the next year. The carry-over is in addition to the new annual grant, so the maximum balance in any year is 15 days. Unused sick leave is not paid out when employment ends, except where state or local law requires it.

Long illness: If you need more than your available sick days, you may be eligible for short-term disability or job-protected medical leave. Contact the leave team early so that they can explain your options and paperwork. Sick leave is confidential; managers receive only the dates of absence.

documents.title: Bereavement Leave Policy
documents.content:
Meridian Labs offers paid bereavement leave to help employees grieve, make arrangements and attend services. Bereavement leave is available from the first day of employment and does not reduce vacation or sick balances.

Immediate family: Employees receive 5 paid working days for the death of an immediate family member. Immediate family means spouse or domestic partner, child (including step, foster and adopted children), parent (including step and foster parents and parents-in-law), sibling, and grandparent.

Extended family: Employees receive 3 paid working days for the death of an extended family member, including aunt, uncle, niece, nephew, cousin, grandchild and sibling-in-law.

Other losses: Employees receive 1 paid day to attend the funeral or memorial of a close friend or colleague. Employees receive 5 paid days following a pregnancy loss, stillbirth, failed adoption or failed surrogacy, whether the employee or the employee's partner experienced the loss.

Travel: An additional 2 unpaid days, or 2 days charged to vacation, are available when travel of more than 300 miles is required. Leave does not need to be taken consecutively and may be used within 90 days of the date of death or memorial service, which allows employees to attend services held later.

How to request: Notify your manager and enter the leave in the HR portal. HR may ask for reasonable verification such as a service announcement, but will never require a death certificate. Managers are expected to respond with compassion and to redistribute urgent work.

documents.title: Parental Leave Policy (Primary and Secondary Caregiver)
documents.content:
Overview: Meridian Labs provides paid parental leave to employees who welcome a child through birth, adoption, foster placement or surrogacy. Employees are eligible after 90 days of employment. The policy applies equally to all genders and family structures.

Primary caregiver leave: The primary caregiver receives 16 weeks of paid leave at 100 percent of base salary. For a birth parent, this leave includes the period of medical recovery from childbirth, so no separate disability pay is added on top of the 16 weeks. Where state paid-family-leave programs or short-term disability pay benefits, the company tops up the benefit so that total pay equals 100 percent of base salary.

Secondary caregiver leave: The secondary caregiver (the other parent or partner who shares caregiving responsibilities) receives 8 weeks of paid leave at 100 percent of base salary. If both parents work at Meridian Labs, each designates their role as primary or secondary and each receives the matching leave amount.

Timing and flexibility: Leave must begin within 12 months of the birth or placement and may be taken in one block or in blocks of at least 2 weeks. Employees should give at least 30 days of notice where possible, or as soon as they know of the event in the case of an unexpected placement or early birth.

Ramp-back program: On returning, employees may work a reduced schedule of 80 percent hours at 100 percent pay for the first 4 weeks. Lactation rooms and paid break time for expressing milk are available at all offices and for remote employees through the equipment stipend.

Benefits during leave: Medical, dental and vision coverage continue with no change in employee premiums. Vacation and sick leave continue to accrue, and stock vesting continues. Bonus eligibility is pro-rated only for unpaid periods, and paid parental leave is counted as time worked. Multiple births or placements count as one event. Contact parental-leave@meridianlabs.example to start a leave plan.

documents.title: Company Holidays and Floating Holidays
documents.content:
Company holidays: Meridian Labs observes 11 paid company holidays each year: New Year's Day, Martin Luther King Jr. Day, Presidents' Day, Memorial Day, Juneteenth, Independence Day, Labor Day, Thanksgiving Day, the day after Thanksgiving, Christmas Day, and one additional company shutdown day on December 24 or December 26, announced each October. When a holiday falls on a Saturday it is observed on the preceding Friday, and when it falls on a Sunday it is observed on the following Monday.

Floating holidays: Each employee receives 2 floating holidays per calendar year to be used for religious observances, cultural celebrations or personal days of significance. Floating holidays are granted on January 1, pro-rated for new hires, and do not carry over. They are not paid out when employment ends.

Work on a holiday: Non-exempt employees who are required to work on a company holiday are paid at 1.5 times their regular rate and receive a substitute day off within 60 days. Customer support staff on holiday rotations receive a premium of $200 for each holiday shift.

Other paid time off: Employees receive up to 3 paid hours to vote when polls are not open outside working hours, paid jury duty for up to 10 working days, and paid military leave for annual reserve training of up to 10 working days. Employees also receive one paid volunteer day per year to support a charity of their choice.

documents.title: Medical and Family Leave (FMLA) Policy
documents.content:
Eligibility: Employees who have worked for Meridian Labs for at least 12 months, have worked at least 1,250 hours in the previous 12 months and work at a site with 50 or more employees within 75 miles are eligible for unpaid, job-protected leave under the Family and Medical Leave Act (FMLA). Some states provide broader protection, and the company follows whichever law is more generous.

Leave entitlement: Eligible employees may take up to 12 weeks of leave in a 12-month period for the birth or placement of a child, for the employee's own serious health condition, or to care for a spouse, child or parent with a serious health condition. Up to 26 weeks of military caregiver leave is available in a single 12-month period. Leave can be taken intermittently or on a reduced schedule when medically necessary.

Pay during leave: FMLA leave is unpaid by law, but employees may use sick days and vacation to receive pay while on leave. Employees who qualify for short-term disability receive 60 percent of base salary for up to 12 weeks, and the company tops this up to 80 percent for the first 6 weeks. Paid parental leave under the Parental Leave Policy runs concurrently with FMLA.

Process: Contact the leave team at least 30 days before foreseeable leave. For emergencies, notify HR as soon as possible. HR will provide eligibility notices and medical certification forms within 5 business days. Health benefits continue during leave on the same terms as for active employees. On return, employees are restored to the same or an equivalent role. Questions about whether a particular condition qualifies should be directed to the leave team, which does not provide medical or legal advice.

documents.title: Medical Insurance Plans and Tiers
documents.content:
Eligibility: Full-time employees working 30 or more hours per week and their eligible dependents (spouse or domestic partner and children up to age 26) are eligible for medical coverage beginning on the first day of the month after the start date. New hires have 30 days to enroll. All other changes are made during annual open enrollment each November or within 30 days of a qualifying life event such as marriage, birth or loss of other coverage.

Three medical tiers are offered through the national network:

Essential HDHP (HSA-eligible): Individual deductible $1,600 and family deductible $3,200. Out-of-pocket maximum $4,500 individual and $9,000 family. After the deductible the plan pays 90 percent. Monthly employee premium: $0 for employee only, $140 for employee plus spouse, $110 for employee plus children and $210 for family.

Balanced PPO: Individual deductible $750 and family deductible $1,500. Coinsurance is 80 percent after deductible. Out-of-pocket maximum $3,500 individual and $7,000 family. Primary care visit copay $30 and specialist copay $50. Monthly employee premium: $65 for employee only, $230 for employee plus spouse, $190 for employee plus children and $340 for family.

Premier PPO: Individual deductible $250 and family deductible $500. Coinsurance is 90 percent after deductible. Out-of-pocket maximum $2,000 individual and $4,000 family. Primary care visit copay $20 and specialist copay $35. Monthly employee premium: $140 for employee only, $330 for employee plus spouse, $290 for employee plus children and $470 for family.

All tiers cover preventive care at 100 percent, include telemedicine visits at no cost, and cap prescription copays at $10 for generic, $40 for preferred brand and $80 for non-preferred brand drugs. The company pays roughly 85 percent of the total premium cost.

documents.title: Dental and Vision Insurance
documents.content:
Dental plans: Employees choose between a Basic Dental plan and an Enhanced Dental plan. Both cover preventive care (cleanings, exams and X-rays) at 100 percent with no deductible. The Basic plan covers basic services such as fillings at 80 percent and major services such as crowns at 50 percent, with an annual maximum benefit of $2,000 per person and a lifetime orthodontia benefit of $1,500. The Enhanced plan covers basic services at 90 percent and major services at 70 percent, with an annual maximum of $3,000 per person and a lifetime orthodontia benefit of $2,500 for children and adults. Monthly employee premiums for employee-only coverage are $8 for Basic and $22 for Enhanced. Dependent coverage premiums are $28 and $55 respectively.

Vision plan: A single vision plan covers one eye exam every 12 months with a $10 copay. Frames are covered up to a $200 allowance every 24 months, and standard lenses are covered in full. Contact lenses are covered up to $200 per year in place of glasses. Laser vision correction is discounted by 15 percent at participating providers. Monthly employee premium is $5 for employee only and $14 for family coverage.

Enrollment: Dental and vision are elected separately from medical coverage. Waiting periods do not apply to preventive care. Orthodontia has a 12-month waiting period. Coverage for dependent children runs to age 26.

documents.title: HSA and FSA Accounts and Company Matching
documents.content:
Health Savings Account (HSA): Employees enrolled in the Essential HDHP can open an HSA. Meridian Labs seeds the account with an annual contribution of $500 for individual coverage or $1,000 for family coverage, deposited in two installments in January and July. The company also matches employee contributions dollar for dollar up to an additional $500 for individual coverage and $750 for family coverage per year. This means the maximum company contribution is $1,000 for individual coverage and $1,750 for family coverage. Total contributions from the employee and company are subject to the annual IRS limit, which includes catch-up contributions for employees aged 55 or older. HSA funds belong to the employee, roll over every year, are portable if you leave the company, and may be invested once the balance exceeds $1,000.

Health Care FSA: Employees enrolled in the Balanced or Premier PPO may elect a Health Care Flexible Spending Account up to the annual IRS limit. The company matches 25 percent of the first $1,000 contributed, for a maximum company match of $250. A rollover of up to the IRS carry-over limit is allowed into the next plan year. Unused balances above that limit are forfeited. You cannot hold a general-purpose Health Care FSA and an HSA at the same time.

Dependent Care FSA: All benefit-eligible employees may contribute up to $5,000 per household each year, pre-tax, to pay for child or elder daycare. There is no company match for the Dependent Care FSA.

Submitting claims: Use the benefits debit card or submit receipts in the benefits portal within 90 days after the end of the plan year.

documents.title: Mental Health Therapy Reimbursement Stipend
documents.content:
Annual stipend: Meridian Labs reimburses up to $1,200 per calendar year for mental health care, regardless of which medical plan you choose. The stipend is available to all benefit-eligible employees from their first day of employment and may be used for sessions for the employee and for covered dependents.

Eligible expenses: Reimbursable costs include copays, coinsurance and out-of-network fees for sessions with a licensed therapist, psychologist, psychiatrist, clinical social worker or licensed counselor. Online therapy platforms and couples or family counseling are also covered. Psychiatric medication management visits qualify. The stipend can cover costs that you would otherwise pay before reaching your deductible.

Not eligible: Wellness apps and meditation subscriptions (see the Wellness Stipend), life coaching, executive coaching, prescription drug costs, and expenses reimbursed by insurance. If insurance reimburses part of a session, you can claim only your out-of-pocket portion.

How to claim: Submit the receipt or superbill showing the provider's name, credentials, the date of service and the amount paid in the Meridian expense portal under the category Mental Health Stipend within 60 days of the session. The claim shows to HR benefits staff only; your manager cannot see the claim, and no diagnosis or session notes are ever requested. Reimbursements are paid with the next payroll cycle. Unused stipend does not roll over. The stipend is taxable only if required by local law.

Employee Assistance Program: Separately from the stipend, all employees and household members can access 6 free confidential counseling sessions per issue through the Employee Assistance Program, available 24/7 by phone.

documents.title: Wellness Stipend and Employee Assistance Program
documents.content:
Wellness stipend: Each employee receives a $50 monthly wellness stipend ($600 per year) to spend on gym memberships, fitness classes, home fitness equipment, meditation and sleep apps, nutrition coaching, and similar well-being activities. Submit receipts in the expense portal within 60 days. Unused monthly amounts do not roll over, but employees may bundle up to three months in a single claim.

Employee Assistance Program (EAP): The EAP is a free and confidential service for employees and their household members. It offers up to 6 counseling sessions per issue, financial and legal consultations of up to 30 minutes, childcare and eldercare referral services and identity theft support. The EAP can be reached 24/7 at the number on the benefits portal. Use of the EAP is never reported to managers.

Preventive health: Annual flu shots, biometric screenings and skin-cancer screenings are offered on site or reimbursed in full. Employees who complete an annual health assessment receive a $100 credit toward the wellness stipend.

Wellbeing days: Meridian Labs observes four company-wide Recharge Fridays each year, announced in January, when the company is closed and employees are not expected to work. Meetings are discouraged on Fridays after 3 p.m.

Life and disability insurance: The company pays the full premium for basic life insurance and accidental death coverage equal to 2 times annual base salary up to $500,000. Long-term disability coverage replaces 60 percent of base salary after a 90-day waiting period.

documents.title: Hybrid Work Schedule Guidelines
documents.content:
Work models: Meridian Labs uses three work models, which are assigned by role at hire and recorded in the HR system: Hybrid-Core, Flexible, and Remote-First.

Hybrid-Core teams: Engineering, Product, Design, Data Science and Customer Success are core teams. Employees on core teams must be in the office 2 days per week. The anchor days are Tuesday and Thursday, so that teams can collaborate in person. The other three days are worked from home or any approved location. Attendance is measured by badge swipes on a monthly average, and employees are considered compliant when they average two or more office days per week.

Flexible teams: Sales, Marketing, Finance, Legal and People teams choose their office days with their manager and are expected to be in the office at least 1 day per week, or on-site with customers.

Remote-First roles: Employees hired into roles listed as Remote-First, or who live more than 50 miles from an office, are not required to attend the office but are invited to quarterly team onsites. The company covers travel and lodging for onsites.

Core collaboration hours: All employees are expected to be reachable between 10 a.m. and 3 p.m. in their time zone. Meeting-free focus blocks are protected on Wednesday mornings.

Temporary exceptions: Managers may waive the in-office requirement for a week for illness, family emergencies or severe weather. Longer exceptions, such as for medical conditions, are handled through the accommodations process with HR.

Work from anywhere: Employees may work from another location in the same country for up to 20 days per year with manager notice, and up to 10 days per year from another country with prior approval from HR and Legal for tax and security reasons.

documents.title: Home Office Setup Allowance ($500)
documents.content:
Allowance amount: Meridian Labs provides a one-time $500 home-office setup allowance to every employee who works from home at least one day per week. New hires must use the allowance within their first 90 days. Employees may claim a $250 refresh allowance every 3 years after the original claim.

What is covered: The allowance covers equipment that makes your home workspace safe, comfortable and productive. Eligible items include external monitors, monitor arms, desks and standing desks, ergonomic chairs, keyboards and mice, laptop stands, webcams, headsets and microphones, desk lighting, footrests, surge protectors and docking stations. Equipment bought with the allowance is owned by the employee.

How to claim: Purchase the item, then submit an expense report in the Meridian expense portal under Home Office Setup with an itemized receipt within 60 days of purchase. Claims under $500 are approved automatically if the items are on the eligible list. Reimbursements are paid in the next payroll cycle.

Splitting purchases: The allowance may be split across multiple purchases until the $500 balance is used. Amounts above $500 are the employee's responsibility, and managers cannot approve exceptions to the cap. Requests for medical or accessibility equipment, such as specialized ergonomic seating, are handled under the accommodations process and are not limited to $500.

Company-issued equipment: Laptops, mobile phones and security keys are issued by IT and remain company property. They are not part of the allowance. Contact IT Service Desk for hardware repairs.

documents.title: Expense Eligibility and Reimbursement Rules for Remote Work
documents.content:
Eligible examples: Yes, you can expense a home monitor. A monitor is an approved item under the Home Office Setup Allowance (up to $500 total, one time, with a $250 refresh every 3 years). Other approved purchases include a desk, ergonomic chair, keyboard, mouse, webcam, headset, laptop stand and desk lamp.

Not eligible: Televisions and gaming monitors marketed primarily for gaming, game consoles, personal tablets and smartphones, printers and ink beyond one basic printer, decorative items, rugs, plants and artwork, household furniture such as sofas or bookshelves, software or app subscriptions (unless pre-approved by IT), repairs to personal equipment, and personal internet upgrades beyond the internet stipend. Items purchased before the employee's start date cannot be reimbursed.

Internet and phone stipend: Employees who work from home at least one day per week receive a $50 monthly stipend for home internet. Employees who use a personal phone for work, with manager approval, receive $30 monthly. These are paid through payroll as part of regular pay and appear separately on your pay statement.

Coworking: Remote-First employees who live far from an office may claim up to $200 per month for a coworking membership with manager approval.

Receipt rules: Receipts must show the vendor, date, itemized description and amount. Credit card statements are not accepted on their own. Claims must be submitted within 60 days of purchase. Claims without a valid receipt are denied unless the amount is under $25. Duplicate claims and fraudulent receipts are violations of the Code of Conduct and may lead to disciplinary action.

Returns: If you return an item you were reimbursed for, notify the expenses team so the amount can be deducted. Questions about whether a specific item qualifies should be sent to expenses@meridianlabs.example before purchase.

documents.title: Remote Work Security and Workspace Requirements
documents.content:
Security requirements: Employees working remotely must use the company VPN when accessing internal systems from public or shared networks, keep company laptops encrypted with disk encryption enabled, lock screens when stepping away and use the company-provided password manager and hardware security key. Company data must not be stored on personal devices or personal cloud accounts. Public Wi-Fi may be used only with the VPN switched on.

Physical workspace: Employees are responsible for maintaining a safe workspace with a reliable internet connection of at least 50 Mbps download. Work-related injuries that happen in your home workspace during working hours are covered by workers' compensation and must be reported to HR within 24 hours.

Confidential calls: Do not take confidential calls in public places. Use headphones when others are within hearing range.

Tax and legal location: Employees must work from the state or country recorded in the HR system. Moving to a different state or country requires 60 days of notice to HR because it can change payroll taxes, benefits eligibility and employment law obligations. Working from another country for more than 10 days per year is not permitted without HR and Legal approval.

Loss or theft: Report a lost or stolen device to the IT Service Desk immediately and no later than within one hour of discovery. The device will be remotely wiped.

documents.title: Bi-Annual Performance Review Cycle
documents.content:
Review cycles: Meridian Labs runs two formal performance cycles each year. The Mid-Year Check-In takes place in June and July. It is developmental, includes self-reflection and manager feedback, and does not produce a rating or affect pay. The Year-End Review takes place in December and January, produces an overall rating, and informs merit increases, bonuses and promotion decisions.

Process: Each cycle has four steps. First, employees complete a self-assessment about goals, impact and growth. Second, employees request peer feedback from three to five colleagues. Third, managers write their evaluation, then calibrate ratings with peer managers and the HR business partner to make sure ratings are consistent across teams. Fourth, managers hold a one-on-one discussion with each employee and share the written review.

Rating scale: Year-End ratings use a five-point scale: 5 Exceptional, 4 Exceeds Expectations, 3 Meets Expectations, 2 Partially Meets Expectations and 1 Does Not Meet Expectations. Roughly 60 percent of employees are expected to be rated 3.

Goals: Employees set quarterly objectives and key results with their manager in the first two weeks of each quarter. Managers hold one-on-one meetings at least every two weeks.

Performance improvement: Employees rated 2 or below are placed on a Performance Improvement Plan (PIP) of 60 to 90 days with clear goals and weekly check-ins. See the Progressive Discipline policy for how a PIP relates to disciplinary steps.

Appeals: Employees who disagree with their rating may submit a written appeal to the People team within 10 business days of receiving it. HR reviews the evidence and replies within 15 business days.

documents.title: Merit Increase Bands
documents.content:
Merit cycle: Annual merit increases are effective on March 1 and are based on the Year-End performance rating. Employees must have started on or before October 1 of the prior year to be eligible for a full merit increase. Employees who started between October 2 and December 31 receive a pro-rated increase.

Merit increase bands by rating: 5 Exceptional receives 6 to 8 percent. 4 Exceeds Expectations receives 4 to 6 percent. 3 Meets Expectations receives 2 to 4 percent. 2 Partially Meets Expectations receives 0 to 1 percent. 1 Does Not Meet Expectations receives 0 percent. Managers choose the exact percentage inside the band based on the employee's position in the salary range (compa-ratio). Employees at the top of their salary range may receive part of the increase as a one-time lump sum.

Cost-of-living adjustments: In addition to merit increases, the company reviews regional cost-of-living adjustments every January. Adjustments, if any, are applied by pay zone and are separate from merit.

Promotion increases: Pay increases due to promotion are separate from merit and are typically 8 to 15 percent, as described in the Promotion Policy.

Pay transparency: Salary ranges for every level are available to employees in the compensation portal. Questions about pay equity may be raised at any time with compensation@meridianlabs.example. Employees are free to discuss their own pay with colleagues; retaliation for pay discussions is prohibited.

documents.title: Annual Bonus Eligibility and Targets
documents.content:
Plan overview: The Annual Incentive Plan rewards employees for company and individual performance during the calendar year. Bonuses are paid by March 15 of the following year.

Targets by level: Target bonus is a percentage of annual base salary earned during the plan year. Levels L1 to L3 have a 5 percent target. Levels L4 and L5 have a 10 percent target. Levels L6 and L7 have a 15 percent target. Directors and above have targets between 20 and 30 percent.

How the payout is calculated: Payout equals base salary earned, times the target percentage, times the company performance multiplier (0 to 150 percent, set by the board each January based on revenue and operating margin goals), times the individual performance multiplier. The individual multiplier is 150 percent for a rating of 5, 125 percent for a rating of 4, 100 percent for a rating of 3, 50 percent for a rating of 2 and 0 percent for a rating of 1.

Eligibility rules: Employees must start on or before September 30 of the plan year to be eligible, and bonuses for employees who start during the year are pro-rated by months worked. Employees must be actively employed on the payout date to receive a bonus. Employees who resign or are terminated for cause before the payout date forfeit the bonus. Employees on approved leave receive pro-rated bonuses, except that paid parental leave counts as time worked.

Sales roles are covered by separate commission plans and are not eligible for the Annual Incentive Plan. Spot bonuses of up to $1,000 may be awarded by managers throughout the year through the Recognition portal.

documents.title: Stock Option Grants and Vesting Schedule
documents.content:
Eligibility: Regular full-time employees receive an initial stock option grant at hire. The grant size is determined by level and is stated in the offer letter and the equity portal. Grants are approved by the board of directors on a monthly basis, and the exercise price is the fair market value on the date of board approval.

Vesting schedule: Stock options vest over 4 years with a 1-year cliff. No options vest during the first 12 months. On the first anniversary of the vesting start date, 25 percent of the grant vests at once (the cliff). The remaining 75 percent vests in equal monthly installments of 1/48 of the total grant over the following 36 months, so that the grant is fully vested after 48 months. Vesting continues only while you are employed. If your employment ends before the one-year cliff, you receive no vested options.

Leaves of absence: Vesting continues during paid leaves, including paid parental leave. Vesting is paused during unpaid leaves of more than 30 days and resumes upon return.

Exercising options: Vested options can be exercised through the equity portal by paying the exercise price. Early exercise of unvested options is not permitted. After you leave the company, you have 90 days to exercise vested options. Employees with 5 or more years of service have an extended window of 12 months.

Refresh grants: High performers rated 4 or 5 in the Year-End Review may receive refresh grants that vest over 4 years without a cliff.

Change of control: Unvested options accelerate only on a double trigger: a change of control of the company followed by termination without cause within 12 months. Tax treatment of options varies by individual; employees should consult a personal tax adviser.

documents.title: Promotion Policy and Career Levels
documents.content:
Promotion cycles: Promotions are considered twice a year, effective April 1 and October 1. Nominations are submitted by managers about 6 weeks before each cycle. Employees may discuss readiness for promotion with their manager at any time and may request a promotion review through the People team.

Eligibility criteria: To be nominated, an employee should have spent at least 12 months in their current level, have received a rating of 3 or higher in the previous two review cycles with at least one rating of 4 or above, and show consistent performance at the next level. Exceptional performers may be nominated earlier with approval from the department head.

Evaluation: Promotion packets include a written case from the manager, examples of impact, peer feedback and input from a skip-level manager. A cross-functional promotion committee reviews packets and ensures consistent standards across teams. Decisions are communicated to employees within 10 business days after committee review.

Pay and level changes: A promotion normally comes with a base salary increase of 8 to 15 percent, which moves the employee to at least the minimum of the new salary range. The bonus target is updated to the new level and is pro-rated for the plan year. A new equity refresh grant may be awarded for promotions to L5 and above.

Career paths: Meridian Labs offers an individual contributor track and a management track. Moving between tracks does not need a promotion. Employees can see the career level guide in the People portal.

documents.title: 401(k) Retirement Plan and Company Match
documents.content:
Plan overview: Meridian Labs sponsors a 401(k) retirement savings plan for all employees aged 18 or older. Employees are eligible on their first day of employment and may choose pre-tax contributions, Roth after-tax contributions, or a mix of both. Employees can also roll over balances from previous employers' plans.

Company match: The company matches 100 percent of the first 3 percent of eligible pay that an employee contributes, plus 50 percent of the next 2 percent of eligible pay contributed. This means that an employee who contributes 5 percent of pay or more receives the maximum company match of 4 percent of eligible pay. For example, an employee earning $100,000 who contributes $5,000 receives a $4,000 company match. The match is deposited every pay period.

Vesting: Company matching contributions are 100 percent vested immediately. Employee contributions are always fully owned by the employee.

Automatic enrollment: New hires are automatically enrolled at a 5 percent pre-tax contribution rate after 30 days, which increases by 1 percentage point each year up to 10 percent unless the employee changes it. Employees can opt out or change their rate at any time in the benefits portal.

Limits: Total employee contributions are limited by the annual IRS elective deferral limit. Employees aged 50 or older may make additional catch-up contributions. Eligible pay includes base salary, bonuses and commissions.

Additional features: The plan offers a range of low-cost index funds and target-date funds, a brokerage window and plan loans. Free one-on-one financial planning sessions are available through the plan recordkeeper. Investment decisions are the responsibility of the employee, and the company does not provide investment advice.

documents.category: Workplace Code of Conduct & Disciplinary Steps
documents.title: Code of Conduct Overview
documents.content:
Purpose: The Meridian Labs Code of Conduct describes how we treat each other, our customers and our partners. It applies to all employees, contractors, interns and board members, in the office, working remotely, at company events and on company systems, and in any online interaction that affects the workplace.

Core principles: We act with integrity and honesty. We treat all colleagues with respect and dignity. We protect confidential information and customer data. We comply with all applicable laws and company policies. We avoid conflicts of interest. We speak up when something seems wrong.

Professional behavior: Employees are expected to communicate respectfully, be punctual and prepared, represent the company well on social media, use company resources only for legitimate business purposes and avoid working under the influence of alcohol or drugs. Falsifying records, expense fraud, theft, workplace violence and threats are prohibited.

Conflicts of interest and gifts: Employees must disclose outside employment, board seats and financial interests in competitors, customers or suppliers to the Ethics team. Gifts and entertainment from business partners above a value of $100 must be reported and may need to be declined. Gifts of cash are never acceptable.

Customer and company data: Employees must protect personal data and confidential information and access it only when needed for work. Data may not be shared outside the company without authorization.

Responsibilities of managers: Managers must model the Code, take every concern seriously, escalate reports of harassment or discrimination to HR within one business day and protect anyone who reports in good faith.

documents.category: Workplace Code of Conduct & Disciplinary Steps
documents.title: Anti-Harassment and Anti-Discrimination Policy
documents.content:
Commitment: Meridian Labs prohibits harassment and discrimination based on race, color, religion, sex, pregnancy, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, national origin, age, disability, genetic information, veteran status, marital status or any other characteristic protected by law. This policy applies to employees, applicants, contractors, customers and vendors, and to conduct at work, at work-related events, online and in chat tools.

What is harassment: Harassment is unwelcome conduct that creates an intimidating, hostile or offensive work environment or that interferes with a person's work. Examples include slurs, offensive jokes, mocking, unwanted touching, sexual advances, sharing inappropriate images, stalking, intimidation and repeated exclusion. Sexual harassment includes unwelcome advances, requests for sexual favors and quid pro quo situations in which employment decisions depend on submission to sexual conduct. A single serious incident can be a violation, and the intent of the person does not change the impact.

Reasonable accommodation: The company provides reasonable accommodations for disability, pregnancy, lactation and sincerely held religious beliefs unless doing so would cause undue hardship. Requests are made to the People team, which handles them confidentially.

Investigations: All complaints are taken seriously and investigated promptly, fairly and as confidentially as possible. HR will acknowledge a report within 2 business days and aims to complete an investigation within 30 days. Both the reporting employee and the person accused are informed of the outcome. Substantiated violations lead to corrective action up to and including termination.

Managers who witness or learn of harassment must report it to HR even if the employee asks them not to. Employees who are uncertain whether conduct is prohibited are encouraged to ask HR. This policy does not provide legal advice; employees may also contact the Equal Employment Opportunity Commission or the corresponding state agency.

documents.category: Workplace Code of Conduct & Disciplinary Steps
documents.title: Non-Retaliation Policy
documents.content:
Policy statement: Meridian Labs strictly prohibits retaliation against anyone who, in good faith, reports a concern, asks a question about policy, participates in an investigation, requests an accommodation or leave, or discusses their pay. This protection applies even if the concern turns out to be unfounded, as long as the report was made honestly.

What counts as retaliation: Retaliation includes termination, demotion, reduced hours or pay, unfavorable reviews, exclusion from meetings or projects, undesirable reassignment, threats, ostracism, spreading rumors, interfering with promotions or any other action that would discourage a reasonable person from reporting. Retaliation by a colleague is treated the same as retaliation by a manager.

Protections: Employees who report concerns are protected from adverse employment actions for at least 12 months after the report. HR checks in with the reporting employee at 30, 90 and 180 days after the case closes to confirm that no retaliation has occurred. Any employee who believes they have faced retaliation should contact ethics@meridianlabs.example or use the confidential hotline right away.

Consequences: Retaliation is a serious violation of the Code of Conduct. Employees who retaliate, or who knowingly make a false report in bad faith, are subject to discipline up to and including termination of employment, without applying earlier steps of the progressive discipline ladder.

Legal rights: Nothing in this policy limits an employee's right to report possible violations of law to a government agency or to participate in agency investigations, and no prior approval from the company is required. Anonymous reports are accepted and protected.

documents.category: Workplace Code of Conduct & Disciplinary Steps
documents.title: Ethics and Compliance Reporting Hotline
documents.content:
Purpose: The Ethics Hotline is a confidential channel for reporting suspected violations of the Code of Conduct, harassment, discrimination, fraud, safety concerns, accounting irregularities, conflicts of interest or retaliation. It is operated by an independent third-party provider so that reports can be made anonymously.

How to report: The hotline is available 24 hours a day, 7 days a week, in more than 40 languages. Call the toll-free number 1-800-555-0142, use the web portal at the address listed on the intranet page named Speak Up, or send an email to ethics@meridianlabs.example. Reports can also be made to your manager, your HR business partner or any member of the Legal team. Reports that involve a manager or HR can be sent directly to the Chief Compliance Officer.

Anonymity: You may choose to report anonymously. You will be given a case number and a PIN so that you can check the status and answer questions from investigators without revealing your identity. The provider does not trace calls or log IP addresses.

What happens next: Reports are triaged by the Ethics team within 2 business days. A trained investigator who has no conflict of interest is assigned, and the report is handled with strict confidentiality shared only with people who need to know. Reporters receive an update at least every 14 days and a closing summary when the case ends. Investigations are normally completed within 30 days.

Protection: All reports made in good faith are protected under the Non-Retaliation Policy. Quarterly summary statistics of reports and outcomes are shared with the Audit Committee of the board.

documents.category: Workplace Code of Conduct & Disciplinary Steps
documents.title: Progressive Discipline Ladder
documents.content:
Philosophy: Meridian Labs uses progressive discipline to help employees correct problems with performance or conduct. The goal is to be fair, consistent and proportionate. Employment at Meridian Labs is at will, which means that either the employee or the company may end employment at any time, with or without cause or notice, and nothing in this policy changes that. The company may skip steps or repeat steps depending on the seriousness of the issue.

The ladder has five steps:

Step 1 - Verbal coaching: The manager meets privately with the employee to explain the concern and the expected improvement. The manager documents the conversation in a coaching note.

Step 2 - Written warning: If the issue continues, or if the first problem is more serious, the manager and HR issue a written warning that describes the issue, the expected improvement, a timeline and the consequences of not improving. The employee signs to acknowledge receipt. Signing does not mean agreement.

Step 3 - Final written warning or Performance Improvement Plan (PIP): A final written warning or a PIP of 60 to 90 days is used when concerns persist. It includes specific goals and weekly check-ins. The employee is informed that further problems may lead to termination.

Step 4 - Suspension: In certain conduct cases the company may place the employee on paid or unpaid suspension of up to 5 working days while a matter is investigated.

Step 5 - Termination: Employment may be terminated if the employee fails to improve or if the misconduct is serious. Terminations require HR and Legal review and the approval of a department head.

Immediate termination: Serious misconduct may lead to immediate termination without prior steps. Examples are violence or threats, harassment, theft, fraud or falsifying expense claims, serious breaches of data security, working under the influence, and retaliation against a reporter.

Employee rights: Employees can bring a written response to the file and request that HR review any disciplinary action within 10 business days. Warnings stay active for 12 months and are removed from the active file if no further issues occur. The company will provide final pay as required by state law.

documents.category: Workplace Code of Conduct & Disciplinary Steps
documents.title: Workplace Safety and Substance Policy
documents.content:
Workplace safety: Meridian Labs is committed to a safe and healthy workplace. Employees must follow all posted safety instructions, report hazards and injuries to their manager and HR immediately, take part in emergency drills and keep walkways and emergency exits clear. Workplace violence, threats, intimidation and weapons on company premises are prohibited, except where law enforcement or licensed security personnel are authorized.

Injury reporting: Work-related injuries or illnesses, including those that happen in a home workspace during working hours, must be reported to HR within 24 hours so that workers' compensation claims can be filed. Employees are never penalized for reporting an injury.

Substance use: Employees may not work while impaired by alcohol, cannabis, illegal drugs or misused prescription drugs. Alcohol may be served at company-approved events, and employees are expected to drink responsibly, and the company offers alternative transportation. Employees who need to use prescription medication that could affect their work are encouraged to speak with HR confidentially; the company will consider reasonable accommodations.

Support and treatment: Employees who struggle with substance use are encouraged to seek help through the Employee Assistance Program before an issue affects their work. Seeking help voluntarily will not lead to discipline, though employees are still expected to meet performance and conduct standards.

Reasonable-suspicion testing: Where there is a reasonable suspicion of impairment, the manager must consult HR, and the employee may be asked to take a test at a certified provider, consistent with applicable law. Refusing a test may result in discipline under the progressive discipline ladder.
